does: Scatters a filling over one half of a thin round of dough, folds the other half over it and presses the edges shut, so that the filling is held in a flat parcel that cooks on a dry griddle.
how: Roll the dough out into a thin, even round and brush off the loose flour.
Scatter a thin layer of filling over one half, leaving a clear rim at the edge.
Lift the clear half over the filling and press the rim with the fingertips until it is sealed all the way round.
Carry the parcel to the hot griddle without letting it stretch.

cues.text: The parcel is a flat half moon with an even bump of filling and a neat, thin rim.
The rim is pressed thin and sticks to itself, with no gap.

mistakes.mistake: Overfilling, so that the parcel bursts on the griddle.
mistakes.fix: Spread the filling in a thin layer.

mistakes.mistake: Using a wet filling, which soaks the dough and makes it soggy.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze or drain a wet filling first.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving flour on the rim, so that it will not stick.
mistakes.fix: Brush the rim clean before pressing it shut.

comes_after.why: The dough must be rolled thin and even before it can be folded over a filling.

variant_of.differs: The dough is folded once over a filling to make a flat sealed parcel, with no layers built up. Folding dough in the layered way stacks sheets over fat.
